item.title: Report: Witkoff and Kushner to travel to Norway for talks with Ukraine
item.description:
US President Donald Trump's envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, are planning to travel to Norway for talks with Ukraine, Reuters reported, citing three sources familiar with the matter.
Two of the sources said Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is also expected to participate in the talks.

item.title: Jewish women punched in face in London antisemitic attacks, suspect arrested
item.description: At least two Jewish women were assaulted in Stamford Hill, with one suffering significant bruising. Police arrested a suspect on suspicion of racially and religiously aggravated grievous bodily harm.

item.title: Suspected terrorist infiltration in Evyatar
item.description:
A short while ago, sirens were sounded regarding a suspected terrorist infiltration in the area of Evyatar.
The IDF stated that it remains in close contact with the local communities and security forces in the region.

item.title: World first? Wounded soldier evacuated from front lines by drone
item.description: Ukraine's military announced that it successfully evacuated a wounded soldier from a combat zone using a heavy-lift drone after minefields and the threat of Russian drones made evacuation by land impossible.

item.title: Sudan: 80 people killed in UAV attack at transporation station
item.description: At least 80 people were killed in a drone attack near a market and a transportation station in the town of A-Dibab in the state of West Kordofan in Sudan. This was reported by the AFP news agency, citing a medical source and an eyewitness. Most of the dead were civilians waiting for transportation home.

item.title: Hazardous materials leak at Intel plant: Emergency forces still working on site
item.description:
Fire and rescue teams continue to operate at the Intel plant following a leak of hazardous materials, in cooperation with police forces, the Ministry of Environmental Protection, and the plant's emergency team.
The forces operating at the scene are formulating an operational plan for further handling of the incident.

item.title: Meyer Habib slams Macron: France is paying the price
item.description: Habib criticizes the Macron administration following riots and looting in France, accuses the authorities of failing to act, and links hostility toward Israel to the crisis gripping the country.

item.title: Report: Qatar to build two power plants in Lebanon and supply it with natural gas for 20 years
item.description: Qatar is expected to build two power plants in Lebanon and sign an agreement to supply liquefied natural gas to the country for 20 years, according to a draft plan for the Lebanese electricity sector obtained by Reuters.

item.title: Foreign Minister Sa'ar speaks with Polish counterpart
item.description:
Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar spoke on the phone on Monday with Poland’s Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, Radosław Sikorski.
The two discussed the significant increase in Israeli tourism to Poland and opportunities to expand cooperation, dialogue, and investment between the countries. In addition, they discussed the war in Ukraine and the situation in the Middle East.
Sa'ar updated Minister Sikorski on the police investigation into the incident in Judea and Samaria involving several diplomats, including the Polish Consul.

item.title: Political bombshell: Benny Gantz withdraws from election race
item.description: Blue and White chairman Benny Gantz announced that he will not run in the upcoming elections.

item.title: Captivity survivor's mother: Netanyahu bears responsibility for nurturing Hamas in Gaza
item.description: The mother of former hostage Avinatan Or blames the Prime Minister for allowing funds to flow to Hamas and for the prolonged war, but stops short of saying he should have resigned.
